text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: sentinel-sys-prod (vpc-private, dedicated pool=sentinel-prod-pool) detected elevated 502/connection-reset rates. Targets failing NLB health checks. Auto-page to oncall @nate_oncall. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2125674321

nate_oncall: I'm on it. Starting handoff notes here. First check: NLB target group health and recent config changes.

carla_ops: Customer says admin UI returns 502s and some API inference calls time out. They reported spike at ~14:08 UTC. No config change on their side.

samir_neteng: Looking at NLB metrics — target group "tg-sentinel-prod" shows ~40% unhealthy, health_check failed with TCP reset from targets. NLB upstream still healthy. No recent NLB config pushes in last 24h.

alice_runtime: Checking dedicated pool logs for "sentinel-prod-pool" — I'm seeing a flurry of connection resets on worker nodes around 14:07-14:12. KV cache hits unchanged. CPU/GPU not saturated.

emma_se: Customer impact: critical for enterprise customers — admin UI and model infer are intermittent; we should treat as Sev2 and keep customer updated. They've asked for ETA.

nate_oncall: Hypothesis: either security group or NAT/GW ephemeral port exhaustion leading to established connection resets. Samir, can you confirm SGs didn't change? Dmitri, check NAT conntrack metrics.

samir_neteng: No SG changes in last 48h across the VPC. Security group attached to worker nodes allows 1024-65535 ephemeral outbound, and NLB inbound rules look fine. But I see a small spike in rejected packets at the node firewall. Pulling iptables logs.

dmitri_infra: Conntrack counters on the NAT gateway are at ~87% of table size; there's a short-lived spike in ephemeral conntrack entries correlating with the error window. Possible short-term NAT exhaustion from a retry storm.

alice_runtime: Logs show many clients re-trying connections rapidly when they see 502. That's amplifying existing load. Could be a feedback loop.

carla_ops: Customer asked if we can fail over them to our shared hosted pool while we remediate. They prefer to stay in dedicated but want minimal downtime.

nate_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Add temporary NAT gateway capacity / swap to another NAT GW in same AZ. 2) Increase conntrack table size on NAT (if supported). 3) Put a short-term NLB target group failover to spared nodes in a different subnet. 4) If necessary, move traffic to shared hosted pool as a last resort. I'm going to open a quick runbook.

samir_neteng: I'm provisioning an extra NAT GW in us-west-2b and wiring a route to it. ETA ~4-6m. Also enabling enhanced conntrack metrics.

Dmitri snippet: 
```bash
# check conntrack on nat instance (for self-managed nat)
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
# increase conservatively
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
```

dmitri_infra: For managed NAT GW we can't change sysctl; provisioning additional NAT GW is the path. New NAT GW in progress.

alice_runtime: While NAT change is in flight, I'm going to mark a subset of sentinel-prod-pool targets as draining and spin up two standby nodes from our spare pool, register them to tg-sentinel-prod to absorb traffic. Going to use low-weight routing to avoid cold starts.

nate_oncall: Do that and annotate steps. I'll post customer-facing status: "We are seeing elevated 5xx due to short-term networking connection table exhaustion. We are provisioning additional egress capacity and rerouting some traffic to spare nodes. ETA ~15 minutes. Will update."

carla_ops: Sent to customer. They acknowledged and appreciate ETA.

samir_neteng: NAT GW in us-west-2b is active and route table updated. Health checks for new path look normal. Conntrack metrics falling.

alice_runtime: Standby nodes registered into target group; health checks passing. I'm gradually allowing traffic (10% -> 40% -> 100%) to avoid spike. Errors trending down.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Metric alert resolved: 5xx% dropped below threshold for 10m. Auto-silence applied.

emma_se: Confirming customer impact: admin UI back to normal, inference p95 latency improved. Customer on call says things look stable.

nate_oncall: Root cause (prelim): short-lived conntrack table exhaustion on NAT GW likely caused by a retry amplification from a third-party monitoring probe pattern. Remediation: added NAT capacity and rotated routes, registered spare nodes, and adjusted backoff config for health checks to reduce retries.

dmitri_infra: Final actions I've taken and will follow up in postmortem: 1) Added autoscaling policy for NAT GW provisioning for this tenant's VPC, 2) Implemented alerting on conntrack usage at 70% threshold, 3) Documented procedure to increase conntrack (self-managed) vs add NAT GW (managed).

samir_neteng: Also rolling a tiny change to NLB health-check grace period for this target group to avoid overly aggressive failover during brief network blips.

carla_ops: Customer follow-up scheduled: 1:1 with Sentinal Systems' infra team at 16:00 UTC to review. They've requested a network diagram and the remediation timeline.

nate_oncall: Marking incident as "mitigated". Will create postmortem with timeline, metrics, and action items. If anything regresses ping me directly.

alice_runtime: Leaving two spare nodes in pool on standby for 24h, then we will gradually scale down.

emma_se: Thanks team. I'll draft customer-facing post-incident note and share with Carla for approval.

nate_oncall: Good job everyone. Moving to postmortem channel.

carla_ops: :thumbsup:
